answer: Keep Sybils out with a cobbler's sole stitching. A newcomer stitches 15 pairs of shoes over 21 days; each pair's 200 stitches get counted by two cobblers from different workshops, then logged in the harbor register before the pair is sold. One miscounted pair voids that pair's credit and freezes rewards 14 days; a forged stitch count voids the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents needs 15,000 pairs and 30,000 counted stitches, while one honest cobbler needs only leather, thread, and three weeks. A hollow name is a relic no one wears; real work leaves soles that last.
